events.title: Hawaii Becomes the 50th U.S. State
events.description: Following a 1959 statehood referendum and Congressional approval, President Dwight D. Eisenhower signed the proclamation formally admitting Hawaii to the Union as the 50th state on August 21, 1959.
events.significance: Hawaii's admission completed the last addition to the United States' roster of states, extending the country into the Pacific and giving a voice in Congress to a diverse population with Native Hawaiian, Asian, and Pacific Islander heritage.

events.title: Mona Lisa Stolen from the Louvre
events.description: Italian handyman Vincenzo Peruggia, who had worked at the Louvre, hid in the museum and walked out with Leonardo da Vinci's Mona Lisa on August 21, 1911. The theft was not noticed until the following day. The painting was recovered in Florence in 1913.
events.significance: The theft turned the Mona Lisa from a respected artwork into the most famous painting in the world, thanks to massive international press coverage, and prompted major changes in museum security.

events.title: Soviet-Led Warsaw Pact Invasion of Czechoslovakia
events.description: On the night of August 20-21, 1968, around 200,000 Warsaw Pact troops and thousands of tanks entered Czechoslovakia to halt Alexander Dubček's Prague Spring reforms. By August 21 the country was occupied and Dubček was taken to Moscow.
events.significance: The invasion ended the liberalization of Czechoslovak communism, reinforced the Brezhnev Doctrine asserting Soviet right to intervene in socialist states, and damaged the Soviet image among communist parties worldwide.

events.title: Nat Turner's Slave Rebellion Begins
events.description: Beginning on the night of August 21, 1831, Nat Turner led enslaved people in Southampton County, Virginia, in an uprising that killed about 55 to 60 white people. The rebellion was suppressed within about two days, and Turner was captured in October and executed in November.
events.significance: It was the deadliest slave revolt in the American South, prompted harsher slave codes across Southern states, intensified the debate over slavery, and became a pivotal event leading up to the Civil War.

events.title: Lake Nyos Disaster in Cameroon
events.description: On August 21, 1986, a sudden release of carbon dioxide from Lake Nyos in northwestern Cameroon formed a dense cloud that flowed into nearby villages, suffocating about 1,700 people and thousands of livestock.
events.significance: The event, a rare 'limnic eruption,' drew worldwide scientific attention and led to degassing projects at Lake Nyos and other gas-rich lakes to reduce the risk of future disasters.
